annotations.title: Read a Hán Nôm page from an image

description:
Read a photo or scan of a Hán Nôm (漢喃) page — a woodblock print, a manuscript, a stele rubbing, a sign — with Nôm Na Việt's own OCR, trained on Vietnamese Hán Nôm. Use this instead of reading the image yourself: general vision models misread Nôm characters as Chinese ones, or invent them.

Pass the image as base64 (a "data:image/...;base64," prefix is fine), at most 7 MB. Vertical text (columns read right to left) is the default; pass mode "horizontal" for text in rows, or "auto" to have it guessed.

Returns the text region by region in reading order, each with its confidence and box, and every character the OCR was unsure of. The result is a machine reading, not a checked text: report the uncertain characters as uncertain, and never substitute a character you think it "should" be. To gloss what was read, pass the text to convert_text and its characters to lookup_character.

Each call reads one page and counts against a per-caller page budget; a busy OCR service answers with how long to wait.

image.description: The page image, base64-encoded (JPEG, PNG or WebP), optionally as a data: URL. At most 7 MB decoded.

mode.description: "vertical" (columns, read right to left; the default), "horizontal" (rows), or "auto" (guessed from the page).

name: ocr_page

box.description: In the uploaded image's pixels, after any EXIF rotation.

uncertain.description: Characters read with confidence below 0.65. index counts code points of this region's text, from 0.

text.description: Every region, in reading order, one per line.

title: Read a Hán Nôm page from an image
